messages:
sam: FYI bringing up Asteria-7B (int4) on staging. Quick smoke shows generation diffs vs fp16 when context > 1024 and batch_size > 1. not reproducible in single-batch runs. anyone seen this phase-warp behavior? :thinking:
kiara: Hm, that rings a bell — we saw similar with a Gemma int4 run where rotary scaling was slightly off after conversion. Can you paste the smallest failing output?
sam: here's a tiny excerpt (token ids redacted):
```
# fp16 output: ... token_A token_B token_C ...
# int4 output:  ... token_A token_X token_C ...
# diff at pos 2 only when batch=4 / cache reuse
```
ben: could be kvcache alignment or tokenizer conversion. did you use our token-remap step in the converter? link to conversion script?
sam: used converter v2 (master) with --preserve-offsets. Tokenizer looks identical by checksum. converter PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/convertors/pulls/392
kiara: two quick hypotheses: 1) rotary scale mismatch across heads after quant packing, 2) batchwise kv packing rounding causes head-offset drift. try forcing rotary scale to 1.0 at runtime to see if it disappears.
anya: also try running with BATCH=2 and compare to BATCH=4 to see if it's linear with batch. if it's only on reuse, insert an explicit cache flush between requests as a control.
ml-bot: CI run 5178901240 for model-onboard/asteria7b-int4 completed — smoke tests: pass, unit-regressions: 2 warnings (embed diff).
sam: I ran per-channel and per-tensor quant variants — both show same symptom. interestingly, disabling continuous batching (no batching) makes the int4 match fp16. so batching+cache seems involved.
ben: can you run a minimal reproducer locally? e.g.
```bash
./tools/run_local_infer.sh --model asteria-7b --quant int4 --batch 4 --context 2048 --seed 42 --flush-cache false
```
capture output to /tmp/asteria-repro.txt and upload.
kiara: also add env ROTARY_TEST_SCALE=1.0001 and ROTARY_TEST_SCALE=0.9999 runs, and a run with ROTARY_FORCE_NORMALIZE=1 — that will tell if tiny scale perturbations flip the behavior.
sam: starting runs now, will upload logs. estimated 35m. leaving the reproducer command in thread.
anya: if this is headwise offset, we should try a debug build that prints per-head rotary multipliers in the runtime. low-overhead instrumentation: add a debug flag --dump-head-scales.
ben: if you can reproduce, we'll bisect to the quant kernel change that introduced this — start from the last known-good tag (2026-02-10) and run the same script.
kiara: good plan. also adding a quick eval on our unit prompt set (rollout/regression) to quantify quality delta if reproduced: https://dash.internal/quality/asteria7b/onboard
sam: uploaded /tmp/asteria-repro.txt and a small binary diff: https://files.internal/asteria/5178901234/repro.tar.gz. will kick off the ROTARY_FORCE_NORMALIZE runs now.
anya: thanks — tagging infra to avoid other jobs stealing GPUs during the bisect @ben @kiara. :pray:
ben: noted, reserving 1xA100. ping here when you have a minimal repro that fails on >1 batch.
sam: will report back in ~40m with initial results. thanks all. :thumbsup:
